gaps.problem: BLOCKING: nothing in the named toolchain produces `crops.json`, yet four acceptance items auto-fail without it. §4 states "`apicheck.mjs` writes them to `<shot>.crops.json` beside every PNG it captures" and "**A shot with no `crops.json` fails items 2, 10, 12 and 20**". But every shot those items grade — `closeup_12.png`, `closeup_22.png`, `street_12.png` (gauntlet), `street_12_rain.png`, `sunset_17p9.png`, `sunrise_6p2.png` (the hand `tools/screenshot.mjs` lines in §4) — is captured by `tools/screenshot.mjs`, which I confirmed writes only `<out>.json` and has no crop output. `apicheck.mjs` captures none of them. So items 2, 10, 12 and 20 fail by construction no matter what the builder ships, and the builder cannot fix it: `tools/` is integrator-only per BUILDER.md. That is four of twenty-two items, including the two highest-value ones (noon shadow contrast, exposure calibration), and it costs a full round the first time builder and critic read the sentence differently.
gaps.fix: Break the circularity explicitly. Add to §4: "The camera is deterministic for a given `?camera=&time=`, so the rects do not have to come from the same process as the PNG. The critic's `shots/environment/r<n>/apicheck.mjs` boots each of the six pinned-crop URLs (`closeup`@12, `closeup`@22, `street`@12, `street`@12&weather=rain, `sunset`@17.9, `sunrise`@6.2), calls `api._debug().cropRects()` at each, and writes `<shot>.crops.json` next to the PNG the gauntlet or screenshot tool already produced. A missing `crops.json` is a critic-side omission and the item is re-graded once the probe is run, never failed against the builder." Then add core request #13 for a `tools/screenshot.mjs --crops` flag so this stops being a per-round chore.

gaps.problem: Item 20's binding ratio is refuted by its own justification paragraph. It anchors `cal_grey` at `118 ± 15` and demands `cal_grey / cal_black ≥ 2.5`, which requires `cal_black ≤ 47`. Two sentences later the same item argues the r2 band was wrong because "a straight sRGB encode of albedo 0.04 is 57" — and 118/57 = **2.07**, well under 2.5. AgX's toe darkens shadows somewhat, but sky ambient on an unshaded 0.04 patch pushes back the other way; realistically the patch lands 50–57 and the ratio lands 2.1–2.4. So the spec fails the item using its own arithmetic, and it does so on the anchor that pins the whole exposure transfer function — the builder will chase it into a crushed frame and trip item 1's `p1 ∈ [6, 30]`.
gaps.fix: Recompute from the stated anchor rather than from the retired r2 numbers. With `cal_grey = 118` and a straight-sRGB `cal_black ≈ 57`, set `cal_grey / cal_black ≥ 1.9` and `≤ 2.6`, and keep `cal_white / cal_grey ≥ 1.7`. State the reasoning inline as the item already does elsewhere: "0.18→118 and 0.04→57 under a straight sRGB encode gives 2.07; AgX's toe may add ~15 %, so the band is 1.9–2.6 and a value outside it means the toe is wrong, not the exposure."

gaps.problem: Item 19 grades "the shadow of a **known 70 m tower**" — but no 70 m tower exists in the spec. §8.3 says only "~30 concrete blocks and towers", gives no heights and no coordinates, and the tower is absent from the `cropRects()` landmark list (`cal_white`/`cal_grey`/`cal_black`/`shadow_patch`/`lit_patch`/`ground_near`). The item then asks for a shadow "4–10 × its height" measured in metres from a PNG with no pixel→metre mapping given, and for "penumbra ≥ 3 px at 40 m distance" without saying 40 m from which camera (`closeup` sits at distance 110). This is the one item where the spec abandons the landmark-pinning discipline it applies rigorously everywhere else, and it is unbuildable and ungradeable as written.
gaps.fix: Add an eighth landmark in §8: "`tower_ref` — a 70 m × 12 m × 12 m tower at world `(-60, 0, 20)`, registered in `cropRects()`." Then regrade item 19 through the probe, not the pixels: `_debug()` exposes the projected base and shadow-tip NDC of `tower_ref`; the critic checks length/height ratio and the ≤5° bearing against `world.weather.sunDir` in world space, and uses the PNG only for the penumbra, restated as "≥ 3 px at 1080p in `closeup_12.png`".

gaps.property: 3 (Numeric) — measurement scale unstated where it decides the outcome
gaps.problem: §4's default sends every unqualified figure to "the PNG downscaled to 480 px wide", and items 2, 10 and 20 state no pixel size — at which scale their crops are too small to measure. From `closeup` at ~110 m the frame spans ~162 m, so at 1080p a 0.7 m calibration patch is ~8 px and at 480 px it is **~2 px**: item 20's "< 0.5 % of patch pixels at 0 or 255" is arithmetically meaningless on four pixels. Item 2's 2 × 2 m patches drop to ~6 px. Item 10 asks for "high-frequency std after subtracting a **16 px** box blur" on a `ground_near` crop that is 141 px at 1080p but only ~35 px at 480 px, where a 16 px blur consumes the crop. `roads.md`, `props.md` and `democity.md` all carry an explicit guard against this ("no per-material statistic is ever taken at this scale"); this spec does not.
gaps.fix: Add one sentence to §4's pinned-crop paragraph: "Every pinned crop (items 2, 10, 11, 12, 20) is cut from the **full-resolution 1920 × 1080 PNG**, not the 480 px reduction — at 480 px a calibration patch is two pixels wide. The 480 px convention applies only to whole-frame and half-frame statistics (items 1, 3, 5, 8, 21)."

gaps.property: 2 (Falsifiable) — an item that fails on another module's code
gaps.problem: Item 16(a) requires that a `?showcase=all` traversal find "no other `Light` anywhere in the graph", but `src/modules/props/render.js:266` currently constructs `new THREE.PointLight(0xffc987, 0, 34, 2)`. The environment builder may not touch `src/modules/props/`, so item 16(a) fails today for work that is not theirs. (`props.md:25-29` does resolve the ARCHITECTURE §12 "real point lights only near camera" conflict in favour of §4, so the spec text is consistent — but the live tree is not, and the item names no escape.)
gaps.fix: Add to item 16(a): "A foreign `Light` found in the graph is a finding against **that** module, not against environment: name the file and line in the report, record item 16(a) as passed-with-note, and the integrator routes it. Environment fails 16(a) only if the extra light is under `ctx.group` or created by `src/modules/environment/`." Note `src/modules/props/render.js:266` by name so the first critic does not rediscover it.

gaps.problem: Item 7's moon constraints nearly exclude each other, in a spec that does this geometry correctly everywhere else. `moonrise` is registered at pitch 0.09 (`src/modules/environment/index.js:335`), so the top of that frame is only **+17.3°** of elevation and frame centre is −5.2°. Item 7 demands the moon be at "elevation 10–25°" *and* "within 20° of frame centre": the 25° ceiling is unreachable, and at 17.3° the moon is already 22.5° from centre, violating the second clause. The satisfiable window is elevation ~10–15° at near-centre azimuth only. The spec did exactly this envelope analysis for items 9, 11 and 22 and skipped it here.
gaps.fix: Do the same arithmetic inline: "At `moonrise` (pitch 0.09) the top of frame is +17.3° and frame centre −5.2°, so the moon must sit at **elevation 10–16° and within 12° of centre in azimuth**. If the ephemeris cannot place it there at 22:00, re-register `moonrise` with a yaw that centres the moon's azimuth and say so in the build report — do not raise pitch above 0.09."

gaps.problem: Five clauses cannot be checked mechanically and will each cost an exchange. Item 4: "≥ 4 **discrete cumulus with closed silhouettes**" and "within each, top-to-base luma difference ≥ 40" — no segmentation rule, so two critics count 3 and 5 from the same PNG. Item 7: "at least 3 brightness tiers" (undefined) and "a milky-way band raising **local mean** by ≥ 4" (window size unstated). Item 8: "rises 20–80 m" from a PNG with no pixel→metre mapping, and "contrast against the sky ≤ 30" in an unnamed unit. Item 9(a): "≥ 3 distinct cloud-shadow patches", "edge transition ≤ 25 m on the ground" (the aerial ground scale varies across frame and is never given) and "darkening the adjacent lit ground by 12–25 %" ("adjacent" undefined). By my count 13 of 22 items are cleanly mechanical; these five plus the four crops.json items are not.
gaps.fix: Define segmentation once in §4 next to the cloud-pixel rule: "A **cloud** is a 4-connected component of cloud pixels of ≥ 900 px at 1080p after a 3 px morphological open; top-to-base is the mean luma of the top 10 % of its bounding-box rows minus the bottom 10 %." Give §4 a ground-scale line for the `aerial` preset (metres per pixel at frame centre, from `cameraState.distance` and fov 45) so items 8 and 9(a) convert. Restate item 8's "contrast ≤ 30" as "|mean luma of the silhouette band − mean luma of the 20 px of sky directly above it| ≤ 30", and item 9(a)'s "adjacent" as "the annulus 10–30 m outside the patch".

gaps.property: 3 (Numeric) — a number that cannot be measured in this environment, with no stand-in named
gaps.problem: Three §5 budget rows have no observation method, which the standard forbids by name ("If a number cannot be measured in this environment, say so explicitly and name what stands in for it"). "GPU texture memory ≤ 120 MB": the screenshot JSON reports `textures` as a **count**, not bytes — I confirmed in `src/core/debug.js:23`. "Init ≤ 3.5 s warm cache": the JSON carries `elapsedMs` for the whole capture, not init, and on a box where one frame takes 2–12 s a 3.5 s init threshold is not resolvable. "Per-frame allocation: none in `update()`": no probe. Separately, item 12's "within **2 s** of `__sim.ready`" uses wall-clock on that same box — item 14 correctly counts frames ("≥ 14 frames per step") and item 12 should too.
gaps.fix: Replace the three rows with checkable ones: texture memory becomes "the builder lists every allocation with its byte size in `docs/builds/environment_r<n>.json` under `textureBytes`, summing ≤ 120 MB; the critic re-derives it from the code, since `stats().textures` is a count"; init becomes "`_debug().initMs`, recorded by the module itself, ≤ 3500"; allocation becomes "a `grep -n 'new THREE\.' src/modules/environment/*.js` shows no constructor inside `update()` or its callees". Change item 12 to "by the 5th rendered frame after `__sim.ready`".

gaps.property: 3 (Numeric) — unpinned value that a graded item depends on
gaps.problem: Item 11 reasons that the top 5 % band of `sunset_17p9.png` "spans elevation 14.7–16.8° ... and is pure sky since the frame is 37.9 % sky" — both figures derive from `sunset`/`sunrise` being at pitch 0.10, which is true in `src/modules/environment/index.js:332,334` but is **not pinned anywhere in §8**. §8's preset table constrains only `sky` ("pitch ≤ 0.12"). A builder who legitimately re-registers `sunset` at pitch 0.25 puts ground in the top 5 % band and fails `B ≥ R + 8` for a reason the item never intended. Relatedly, §8.6/§8.7's off-axis angles are **horizontal-only**: I get 1.5° horizontal but −11.2° vertical for `shadow_patch`, and 6.5° horizontal but −16.4° vertical for `ground_near`, which puts `ground_near` at ~86 % down the `closeup` frame — in frame, but not the "near frame centre" the text implies.
gaps.fix: Add a pitch column to §8's preset table pinning `sunset` 0.10, `sunrise` 0.10, `moonrise` 0.09, `sky` ≤ 0.12, with the same "restate the request in `docs/core-requests/environment.md`" clause item 22 already carries. In §8.6/§8.7 label the angles "horizontal (azimuthal) off-axis" and add the vertical figures, so nobody expects these crops near the optical centre.

strengths: Factual accuracy is exceptional and I could not break it by spot-check. Every file:line citation resolves: `src/core/world.js:85` (the 0.0006 pre-init default), `src/modules/environment/index.js:15-21` (the five presets, values match the table exactly), `src/modules/environment/shaders.js:145-155` (the nine uEnv* uniforms, all nine present in `addEnvUniforms`), `src/core/camera.js:9` (fov 45) and `:16` (minPitch 0.08), `tools/gauntlet.mjs:18,21` (the no-weather-suffix filename and the unguarded `--weather` forward — the overwrite hazard is real), `tools/screenshot.mjs:101` (`cameraState: perf.camera`).

The geometry is not decorative — it is correct. I recomputed it independently: `clock.sunElevation(12)` = sin(π/2)×(π/2)×0.72 = 1.131 rad = **64.8°** exactly as claimed; shadow length h/tan(64.8°) = **0.47h** exactly; the canopy's 2.8 m −Z offset is right, and −Z is correctly derived from ARCHITECTURE §2's −Z-north convention. Every sky-fraction in the §4 table checks out against `y_h = H/2×(1−tan(pitch)/tan(22.5°))`: aerial 0.0 %, skyline 30.5 %, street 28.0 %, closeup 5.9 %, sky 35.4 %, minPitch ceiling 40.3 % and +17.9°. The 26.2° aerial overshoot and the 11.7 m/texel cloud-shadow figure are both right.

The landmark distances are computed from the real camera basis in `src/core/camera.js:80-88`, not guessed: I reproduced `ground_near` at **73.8 m** from `closeup` (spec: ≈74 m) and **43.5 m** from `street` (spec: ≈43 m). Item 14's sun-direction assertions also verify numerically — x = 0.981 at 06:30, y = 0.905 at 12:00, x = −0.981 at 17:30.

Property 10 is best-in-class. Every §6 failure mode and every `(rN rank M)` citation maps to a real entry in `docs/critic/environment_r1.json` / `_r2.json` — r2 ranks 1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and r1 ranks 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13 all match by rank and by content. The inline measurements are quoted from the reports verbatim (aerial_12 p99 118 / std 17, skyline_17p5 mean 151 / p50 152 / p99 247, wetness 0.065). Nothing generic, nothing invented.

§2 copies the ARCHITECTURE §3 `weather` block verbatim rather than paraphrasing, and then does something better than most specs: it verifies the integrator's decision log against §3, finds the log wrong (§3 really does end at `skyLight` — confirmed), says so, and declares itself the interim contract for the nine extra fields. It correctly reads `?pitch=` as declined despite `camera.js:16`'s stale comment claiming otherwise — no pitch parsing exists in `src/main.js`, `src/core/showcase.js` or `tools/`.

Every named dependency API exists with the stated signature: `clock.sunAzimuth/isNight`, `camera.registerPreset/flyTo/enableControls/screenToGround`, `assets.pbr/applyPbr/texture/hdri/gltf/procedural.*` including `armMap`, `rng.weighted/gauss/fork`, `QUALITY.high = {cascades:3, shadowMap:2048}`, `RENDER_ORDER.SKY = -1000`, `__sim.stats().moduleMs`, and `?showcase=all` (`src/main.js:40`). The §7 warning that ARCHITECTURE §6 is stale is itself correct.

Correct role-file hygiene, and self-aware about it: §6's last bullet explicitly states which SwiftShader invariants were *removed* from this spec because they belong in BUILDER.md/CRITIC.md. Blast radius, anti-inflation, autonomy and the 0–10 anchors are all left to the role files rather than duplicated. The module-specific liveness rule ("never run the gauntlet with `--weather`") is genuinely module-specific and earns its place.

Item 20 openly retires its own predecessor as over-constrained and switches from absolute bands to ratios — exactly the anti-inflation reflex the standard asks for, applied to the spec's own prior text.
verdict:
8.0 — fails at 8.5, but it is a near miss from an unusually rigorous document, and the fixes are one editing pass rather than a rewrite.

This is the most factually reliable module spec I have audited in this repo. I tried to break it and mostly could not: every file:line citation resolves, all five weather presets match `index.js:15-21` exactly, all nine `uEnv*` uniforms exist in `shaders.js`, and every dependency API I checked (`clock.sunAzimuth/isNight`, `camera.registerPreset/screenToGround`, `assets.pbr/applyPbr/armMap`, `rng.weighted/gauss/fork`, `QUALITY.high`, `RENDER_ORDER.SKY`, `__sim.stats().moduleMs`, `?showcase=all`) is real with the stated signature. The geometry is not ornamental — I recomputed `sunElevation(12)` = 64.8°, the 0.47h shadow ratio, all seven sky fractions from the horizon formula, and the 74 m / 43 m landmark distances from the actual camera basis in `camera.js:80-88`, and they are right. The §3 block is copied verbatim, and §2 goes further by catching the integrator's decision log claiming §3 documents nine fields it does not. §6's failure modes map one-to-one onto real r1/r2 critic ranks with the reports' own measurements quoted. Properties 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 are met without reservation, and the role-file boundary is respected consciously.

It fails on the two lenses, not on the writing. As a builder I hit seven real guesses, two of them blocking: nothing in the named toolchain produces the `crops.json` that items 2, 10, 12 and 20 declare mandatory, and `tools/` is closed to me — so four of the highest-value items are unwinnable by construction; item 19 grades "a known 70 m tower" that the spec never stages, coordinates, or registers as a landmark; and item 20 demands `cal_grey/cal_black ≥ 2.5` two sentences after arguing that 0.04 albedo sRGB-encodes to 57, which with its own 118 anchor gives 2.07. As a critic I can mechanically settle 13 of 22 items; four are blocked on the missing artifact and five carry a clause ("discrete cumulus with closed silhouettes", "3 brightness tiers", "rises 20–80 m", "edge transition ≤ 25 m on the ground", "adjacent lit ground") that I would have to adjudicate. Two competent builders would ship different modules on item 19, on the black patch, and on the moon.

Two failure classes are worth naming because the spec is otherwise so careful about exactly them. First, scale: §4 defaults everything to 480 px, at which item 20's calibration patches are two pixels wide and item 10's 16 px blur eats its own crop — `roads.md`, `props.md` and `democity.md` all carry a guard against this and this one does not. Second, envelope arithmetic: the spec derives the framing envelope beautifully for items 9, 11 and 22, then skips it for item 7, where `moonrise`'s +17.3° ceiling and the "within 20° of centre" clause nearly exclude each other.

Fix the crops.json circularity, pin `tower_ref`, recompute item 20's ratio from its own anchor, state that pinned crops are cut at 1080p, and give item 7 the envelope treatment the rest of the document already models — that is a 9.
